title: Effectivity of compatible local stack-moduli presentations
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\mathcal X/k$ an algebraic stack. Let $(g_j:\mathcal X_j\to\mathcal X)_{j\in J}$ be a small jointly surjective family of representable separated etale stabilizer-preserving morphisms. For each $j$ let $f_j:\mathcal X_j\to M_j$ be a uniform categorical morphism to an affine $k$-scheme, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and a universal homeomorphism, inducing a bijection $\pi_0(\mathcal X_j(\Omega))\simeq M_j(\Omega)$ for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. Suppose that, for each pair $(i,j)$, the overlap $\mathcal X_{ij}=\mathcal X_i\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_j$ has a uniform categorical morphism $f_{ij}:\mathcal X_{ij}\to M_{ij}$ to a $k$-scheme, and that its two projection squares with $f_i,f_j$ are 2-cartesian, with separated etale bottom maps $M_{ij}\to M_i,M_j$. Then the induced maps from $V=\coprod_{i,j}M_{ij}$ to $W=\coprod_j M_j$ define an etale equivalence relation. Its fppf sheaf quotient $Q=W/V$ is an algebraic space; $M_j\to Q$ form an etale surjective cover and $M_i\times_Q M_j\simeq M_{ij}$. There is a morphism $q:\mathcal X\to Q$, with $qg_j$ equal to $f_j$ followed by $M_j\to Q$, whose squares with every $f_j$ are 2-cartesian. The morphism $q$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and a universal homeomorphism, and $\pi_0(\mathcal X(\Omega))\to Q(\Omega)$ is bijective for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. Stabilizer-preserving means that the map on inertia is an isomorphism after pullback, where inertia parametrizes objects with automorphisms. Algebraic stacks have the meaning in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and algebraic spaces have the meaning in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Stacks in groupoids and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; a 2-fibre product retains the specified isomorphism between the two images of an object. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], large enough for the small coproducts, and interpret $\pi_0$ as isomorphism classes in the indicated fibre groupoid. Algebraically closed extensions use [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The point space of an algebraic stack consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism and common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth surjective scheme atlas. A morphism is a universal homeomorphism if every base change by an algebraic stack induces a homeomorphism of these point spaces. Quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms have the meaning of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]; in particular quasi-separatedness requires a quasi-compact and quasi-separated relative diagonal, tested on scheme charts. A morphism $f:\mathcal Z\to M$ to an algebraic space is uniform categorical if, for every flat algebraic-space map $M'\to M$ and every algebraic space $T/k$, composition with $f_{M'}$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Mor}_k(M',T)$ to $\operatorname{Mor}_k(\mathcal Z\times_M M',T)$. Etale and separated are tested on scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], and flatness uses [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The sheaf quotient is the fppf sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $T\mapsto W(T)/V(T)$.

proof.text: Fix $i,j,k$. Write $P_{ijk}=M_{ij}\times_{M_j}M_{jk}$ and $\mathcal X_{ijk}=\mathcal X_i\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_j\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_k$. These are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. The assumed cartesian squares identify $\mathcal X_{ijk}$ with $\mathcal X_{ij}\times_{M_{ij}}P_{ijk}$: both describe a triple together with its two consecutive isomorphisms. The map $P_{ijk}\to M_{ij}$ is etale, hence flat, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Thus the definition of uniform categorical applied to $f_{ij}$ supplies a categorical map $\mathcal X_{ijk}\to P_{ijk}$. Compose the outer projection with $f_{ik}$ and factor uniquely to obtain $c_{ijk}:P_{ijk}\to M_{ik}$. Uniqueness makes its two maps to $M_i,M_k$ the outer projections. Likewise factor $\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X_{ii}\to M_{ii}$ through $f_i$ to obtain $e_i:M_i\to M_{ii}$, and factor $\mathcal X_{ij}\to\mathcal X_{ji}\to M_{ji}$ through $f_{ij}$ to obtain the flip. Their endpoint equalities follow by precomposition with the categorical maps. Take the small scheme coproducts of these maps using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. They give $e:W\to V$, $i:V\to V$, and $c:V\times_{t,W,s}V\to V$ over the diagonal, flip and outer projection. The two maps $s,t:V\to W$ are etale, since this is their given property on each open component.

For an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, objects of $\mathcal X_{ij}(\Omega)$ are $(x_i,x_j,\alpha:g_ix_i\simeq g_jx_j)$. Their isomorphism classes map onto $\pi_0\mathcal X_i(\Omega)\times_{\pi_0\mathcal X(\Omega)}\pi_0\mathcal X_j(\Omega)$: equality of classes is exactly existence of $\alpha$. This map is injective: first use isomorphisms of $x_i,x_j$ to fix both objects; two choices $\alpha,\beta$ then differ by $\beta^{-1}\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(g_ix_i)$, which lifts to $\operatorname{Aut}(x_i)$ by stabilizer preservation. This gives an isomorphism of the triples. The cartesian identification $\mathcal X_{ij}\simeq\mathcal X_i\times_{M_i}M_{ij}$ and the assumed bijection for $f_i$ also give $\pi_0\mathcal X_{ij}(\Omega)\simeq M_{ij}(\Omega)$: the fibre groupoid at a fixed $m_{ij}$ is the nonempty single-isomorphism-class fibre of $f_i$. Consequently $V(\Omega)=W(\Omega)\times_{\pi_0\mathcal X(\Omega)}W(\Omega)$ as a subset of $W(\Omega)^2$. It is the kernel equivalence relation of a function, including when some schemes are empty.

Apply [lem-sfb-unramified-geometric-equivalence-relation] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: step 1 supplies the endpoint-compatible $e,i,c$ and etale projections, and step 2 supplies the required geometric equivalence relation. Thus $V\to W\times_kW$ is a monomorphism and an equivalence relation on all scheme-valued points. Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] to this small scheme relation. Its fppf sheaf quotient $Q$ is an algebraic space, $W\to Q$ is etale surjective, and $V\simeq W\times_QW$. Restricting this last isomorphism to the open components indexed by $(i,j)$ gives precisely $M_{ij}\simeq M_i\times_QM_j$, with the specified two maps. The component maps $M_j\to Q$ therefore form a jointly surjective etale family.

For $a\in\mathcal X(T)$, pull back the covering $\mathcal X_j\to\mathcal X$ to obtain jointly surjective representable etale algebraic-space maps $T_j\to T$. Refine these by etale scheme charts; base change, composition and surjectivity are supplied by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. On each such scheme $E\to T_j$ the tautological lift $a_j$ gives $E\to M_j\to Q$. For two lifts the specified isomorphism to $a$ gives a map from their scheme overlap to $\mathcal X_{ij}$; its map to $M_{ij}$ shows that the two $Q$-sections agree. Since $Q$ is an fppf sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space], these sections glue uniquely to $q(a)\in Q(T)$. An isomorphism $a\simeq a'$ identifies the two constructions on a common covering refinement, so gives the same section. Pulling back along $T'\to T$ pulls back this entire compatible family; uniqueness of sheaf gluing gives $q(a)|_{T'}=q(a|_{T'})$. Thus $q$ is a morphism of stacks to the discrete groupoid $Q$. When $a$ comes from $\mathcal X_i$, its given $f_i$-section agrees with the constructed local sections on this cover, so $qg_i=(M_i\to Q)f_i$.

Set $\mathcal Y_i=\mathcal X\times_Q M_i$ and let $h_i:\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal Y_i$ be the comparison from step 4. Pull it back along $\mathcal X_j\to\mathcal X$. By step 3 its target becomes $\mathcal X_j\times_{M_j}M_{ij}$, and its source is $\mathcal X_i\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_j=\mathcal X_{ij}$. The resulting map is the equivalence in the assumed projection square, respecting the specified maps. These pullbacks cover every object of $\mathcal Y_i$ on an etale scheme cover, by the chart calculus. Hence $h_i$ is fully faithful on each fibre: on such a cover its maps of isomorphism sheaves are bijections; local inverse isomorphisms glue uniquely because both sides are stacks: $\mathcal X_i$ by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and $\mathcal Y_i$ because the algebraic space $Q$, regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid with its etale scheme atlas, is an algebraic stack, so the 2-fibre product $\mathcal X\times_QM_i$ is an algebraic stack by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. The same local equivalences give local essential surjectivity. Applying [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] to these etale stacks proves $h_i$ an equivalence over schemes. This proves each required 2-cartesian square; it does not assume that the diagonal of $\mathcal X$ is separated.

Apply [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism] to $q$ and the small jointly surjective etale family $M_i\to Q$ from step 3. Step 5 identifies each pullback with the given $f_i$. Each $f_i$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and a universal homeomorphism by hypothesis, using exactly the definitions in the locality lemma. Therefore $q$ has these same three properties. No assertion of finite inertia, separatedness or adequacy is used.

Fix an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. A jointly surjective representable etale family has lifts of $\Omega$-points over the same field: take etale scheme charts of its algebraic-space pullbacks to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. Apply this first to $M_i\to Q$. Every point of $Q(\Omega)$ lifts to $M_i(\Omega)$ and then to an object of $\mathcal X_i(\Omega)$ by the hypothesis on $f_i$; hence it lies in the image of $q$. For injectivity, lift two objects of $\mathcal X(\Omega)$ to $\mathcal X_i(\Omega)$ and $\mathcal X_j(\Omega)$ in the same manner, using the cover $g_i$. If their $q$-images coincide, step 3 gives a unique point of $M_{ij}(\Omega)$ with the two prescribed local images. Step 2 identifies this with an isomorphism class in $\mathcal X_{ij}(\Omega)$ with those local classes, and hence with an isomorphism between the two original objects in $\mathcal X(\Omega)$. This proves the claimed bijection.
